title: Yara and the Harbor
premise: In 1848, as the Republic of Vessany collapses, Yara Solenne, keeper of the last harbor lighthouse, shelters Dominic Ravensworth, a courier carrying coded dispatches that could rewrite who betrayed the republic. When winter closes the bridge and occupying forces arrive to seize the archives, Yara must choose between her sworn neutrality and the found family of refugees hiding in her light-station. Together they smuggle the truth onto the record before the victors' historians can burn it. Dominic escapes by sea with the dispatches; Yara stays behind, inheriting not the harbor but the story itself.
about_author: Lena Sandoval is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters from besieged port towns before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted pilot house on the northern coast, where the fog still dictates her working hours.

chapters.title: The Light Before the Bridge Falls
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. As revolution reaches the coast, Yara keeps the lighthouse burning for ships that no longer answer to any flag. Dominic Ravensworth arrives half-drowned, clutching a sealed courier case, pursued by riders from both armies. When the season's last bridge closes behind them, they are trapped together with a handful of refugee families. The beat is wary hospitality hardening into shared purpose.

chapters.title: What the Archives Owe
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Yara and Dominic. Dominic reveals the dispatches name the ministers who sold the republic, and that the victors' historians arrive within weeks to sanitize the record. Yara's dead father's ledger surfaces, showing he once hid documents in the light-station walls — an inheritance she never knew she carried. Refugees begin copying pages by lamplight. The beat is reluctant trust deepening into love neither will name.

chapters.title: The Season of No Ships
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. An occupying officer quarters himself at the station, charming and watchful, and begins searching room by room. A refugee boy is caught with a copied page, forcing Yara to trade her father's silver to buy silence. Dominic realizes escape by sea is their only chance, but the ice field blocks the harbor mouth. The beat is terror braided with tenderness on the eve of action.

chapters.title: The Record Remains
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, closing with Dominic's letter. During the officer's farewell dinner, Yara triggers the old lighthouse mechanism to mask the sound of Dominic's sledge crossing the ice toward a waiting ship. The dispatches reach the neutral press; the historians' version cracks within a year. Yara remains, keeper now of an archive and a family that chose her. The beat is grief transmuted into inheritance.
